newsitem.title: UK: S&P affirms Romania ratings, outlook stable.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms Romania ratings, outlook stable.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it affirmed ratings for the Republic of Romania and the National Bank of Romania and that the outlook on the ratings remained stable.
S&P said in a statement Romania's BB minus foreign currency and BBB minus local currency long-term ratings were affirmed.
S&P said Romania's ratings were constrained by --
-- a fragile liquidity position with foreign exchange reserve coverage of the financing gap at a very low 11 percent at year end 1996,
-- significant structural weaknesses in the economy,
-- last year's imprudent pre-election economic management, with an increase in the central bank's quasi-fiscal activity,
-- and the challenges of sustaining the political support for economic reform given low per capita income and a history of harsh economic policies.
The agency said the ratings were supported by --
-- improved prospects for tighter financial policies and accelerated structural reforms under a new government, and
-- The anticipated resumption of International Monetary Fund and World Bank lending, which would improve Romania's liquidity position and support key structural reforms.
"The BBB minus local currency rating reflects the government's stronger capacity to service its low Romanian lei debt burden, equal to just about six percent of GDP," S&P said.
It said the stable outlook reflected expectations the new political leadership wanted to address structural problems.

"Failure to adhere to the ambitious austerity programme -- a possibility given the potential for negative social reactions as the programme requires tough and unpopular measures -- and secure international support would likely result in downward credit pressure," S&P said.

"While the moderate, albeit rising, external debt burden may afford some flexibility over the medium term, the short maturity structure and the country's low foreign exchange reserves pose considerable risks if there is any significant deviation from the austerity programme," the agency said.
